# bipluk — Comprehensive Technical & Knowledge Specification (llms-full.txt)

> The browser-native cloud librarian and patch preservation vault for vintage hardware synthesizers. Back up, organize, audit, and recall SysEx banks from 1980s, 1990s, and 2000s hardware synthesizers directly in your web browser via Web MIDI. No desktop drivers, no operating system installation, zero configuration. 100% customer-funded and bootstrapped by Half Radiation LLC.

Website: https://bipluk.com/
Canonical Documentation: https://bipluk.com/llms.txt
Full Specification: https://bipluk.com/llms-full.txt
OpenAPI Schema: https://bipluk.com/openapi.json
MCP Server Card: https://bipluk.com/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json
Agent Skills Index: https://bipluk.com/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json

---

## 1. Core Architecture & Proprietary Technologies

- **Browser-Native Web MIDI (BIPLUK Engine™):**
  Uses the W3C Web MIDI API (`navigator.requestMIDIAccess({ sysex: true })`) to establish direct bidirectional bit-exact hardware connections to physical synthesizer memory banks inside Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and Chromium-based browsers.
- **Adaptive Flow Control & Pacing (BIPLUK Pacing Protocol™):**
  Vintage synthesizers (Yamaha DX7, Roland Juno-106, Korg M1) run on 8-bit CPUs clocked between 2 MHz and 12 MHz (e.g. Motorola 6800/6809, Intel 8031/8051, Zilog Z80). Standard MIDI baud rate is strictly 31,250 bps. Modern USB MIDI interfaces flood the DIN bus with unthrottled buffers, causing immediate MIDI Buffer Overrun errors (ERR 04 / Checksum Failure). Bipluk chunks SysEx payloads into 64-byte packets spaced with adaptive 25ms-60ms delays (`midiOutput.send(data, performance.now() + offset)`), guaranteeing zero lost bytes.
- **Real-Time Hex & SysEx Parser (BIPLUK Real-Time Hex Parser™):**
  Inspects binary `.syx` files on the fly, decoding manufacturer identification IDs, model bytes, patch registers, and packed 7-bit ASCII preset names without server roundtrips.
- **Cloud Vault (BIPLUK Vault™):**
  Encrypted byte-for-byte cloud preservation in PostgreSQL. Protects private synth sound banks against hardware memory loss caused by soldered CR2032 lithium backup battery depletion.
- **1-Click Hardware Recall:**
  Flashes complete 32-, 64-, or 100-patch sound banks back into synthesizer RAM registers in one operation.

---

## 2. Hardware Synthesizer Supported Catalog & Memory Protect Bypass Routines

### Yamaha DX7 (1983)
- **Architecture:** 6-Operator Frequency Modulation (FM), 32 Algorithms, 12-bit DAC (BA9221).
- **URL:** https://bipluk.com/dx7 (also: https://bipluk.com/yamaha-dx7)
- **Memory Protect Bypass:**
  1. Press FUNCTION, then press button 8.
  2. Press button 8 repeatedly until screen reads `MIDI CH = 1`.
  3. Press FUNCTION, then press button 11.
  4. Press 11 repeatedly until screen reads `SYS INFO IR`. Change to `SYS INFO AV` (Available) using the YES/+1 key.
  5. Press INTERNAL, then press button 14 (MEMORY PROTECT).
  6. Press button 14 again to toggle from `ON` to `OFF` using the NO/-1 key.
  7. DX7 is now unlocked for 32-patch 4,096-byte bulk SysEx dump and recall.

### Roland Juno-106 (1984)
- **Architecture:** 6-Voice Digitally Controlled Analog (DCO), 80017A VCF/VCA modules, Stereo Analog BBD Chorus.
- **URL:** https://bipluk.com/juno-106 (also: https://bipluk.com/roland-juno-106)
- **Memory Protect Bypass:**
  1. On the rear panel, slide the MEMORY PROTECT switch to `OFF`.
  2. Locate the MIDI FUNCTION switch (rear panel) and slide to position `III (3)`. Position III enables SysEx communication (I and II only transmit Note and Patch Change data).
  3. Juno-106 is now ready for bidirectional manual and bulk SysEx transfers.

### Korg M1 (1988)
- **Architecture:** 16-bit AI Synthesis Engine PCM Sample Playback & Workstation.
- **URL:** https://bipluk.com/m1 (also: https://bipluk.com/korg-m1)
- **Memory Protect Bypass:**
  1. Press GLOBAL to enter Global Mode.
  2. Press PAGE + until Page 5 (MIDI GLOBAL).
  3. Set `MIDI EXA` (Exclusive Allow) to `ENA` (Enabled).
  4. Press PAGE + to reach Page 6 (MEMORY PROTECT).
  5. Set both `PROG` (Program) and `COMBI` (Combination) to `OFF`.

### Roland Jupiter-6 (1983)
- **Architecture:** 6-Voice Multi-Mode Analog Polyphonic, Dual CEM3340 VCOs, 24dB/12dB Resonant Filter.
- **URL:** https://bipluk.com/jupiter-6 (also: https://bipluk.com/roland-jupiter-6)
- **Memory Protect Bypass:**
  1. Locate the TAPE MEMORY PROTECT switch on the rear panel and slide to `OFF`.
  2. If using the Europa MIDI modification, enter the Europa setup menu and set SysEx Rx/Tx to `ON`.

### Casio CZ-101 (1984)
- **Architecture:** Phase Distortion (PD) Synthesis, Dual DCO/DCW/DCA Envelopes.
- **URL:** https://bipluk.com/cz-101 (also: https://bipluk.com/casio-cz-101)
- **Memory Protect Bypass:**
  1. Toggle the rear recessed PROTECT switch to `OFF`.
  2. Press MIDI button on front panel, verify Basic Channel matches, and confirm SysEx filter is disabled.

### Roland D-50 (1987)
- **Architecture:** Linear Arithmetic (LA) Synthesis, 32 partials, PCM Attack transients + sampled sustain loops.
- **URL:** https://bipluk.com/d-50 (also: https://bipluk.com/roland-d-50)
- **Memory Protect Bypass:**
  1. Press and hold TUNE/FUNCTION, then press MIDI.
  2. Scroll to `PROTECT` setting and change to `OFF`.
  3. Scroll to `EXCLU` (System Exclusive) and set to `ON`.

### Sequential Circuits Prophet-5 (1978 / 2020)
- **Architecture:** 5-Voice Analog Polyphonic, Curtis CEM / SSM VCOs, 4-pole Lowpass Filter.
- **URL:** https://bipluk.com/prophet-5 (also: https://bipluk.com/sequential-prophet-5-rev4)
- **Memory Protect Bypass:**
  1. On Rev 4, press GLOBALS, scroll to MIDI SysEx, set to `All` or `SysEx Dump/Load: On`.
  2. On Rev 3.3, toggle rear memory protect switch to `OFF`.

### Sequential Circuits Prophet-600 (1982)
- **Architecture:** First MIDI Synthesizer, Dual CEM3340 VCOs, Stock Z80 or GliGli high-speed microcontroller mod.
- **URL:** https://bipluk.com/prophet-600 (also: https://bipluk.com/sequential-prophet-600)
- **Memory Protect Bypass:**
  1. Flip the MEMORY PROTECT switch on the front panel to `OFF`.
  2. On GliGli firmware, press TUNE and verify MIDI SysEx RX is enabled.

### Oberheim Matrix-1000 (1988)
- **Architecture:** 1,000 Patches, Dual CEM3396 Curtis Voice-on-a-Chip, Analog 24dB LPF.
- **URL:** https://bipluk.com/matrix-1000 (also: https://bipluk.com/oberheim-matrix-1000)
- **Memory Protect Bypass:**
  1. Press SELECT until the `Bank/Protect` LED lights up.
  2. Press `+` or `-` until display reads `U F` (Unprotected) rather than `P F` (Protected) for user RAM banks (000-199).

### Yamaha TX81Z (1986)
- **Architecture:** 4-Operator FM, 8 Waveforms, Home of the legendary Lately Bass preset.
- **URL:** https://bipluk.com/tx81z (also: https://bipluk.com/yamaha-tx81z)
- **Memory Protect Bypass:**
  1. Press PLAY/PERFORM, then press UTILITY repeatedly until screen displays `Mem Protect`.
  2. Press NO/OFF to set `Mem Protect: OFF`.
  3. Scroll to MIDI parameters and set `Exclusive: ON`.

### Roland Juno-60 (1982)
- **Architecture:** 6-Voice DCO Analog Polyphonic with IR3109 Filter, DCB / Minerva / Tubbutec MIDI Retrofit.
- **URL:** https://bipluk.com/juno-60 (also: https://bipluk.com/roland-juno-60)
- **Memory Protect Bypass:**
  1. Slide rear MEMORY PROTECT switch to `OFF`.
  2. Enter retrofit configuration (e.g. hold LFO TRIG on Tubbutec) to enable SysEx RX.

### Korg Wavestation (1990)
- **Architecture:** Advanced Vector Synthesis, Wave Sequencing, 32-Voice PCM.
- **URL:** https://bipluk.com/korg-wavestation (also: https://bipluk.com/wavestation)
- **Memory Protect Bypass:**
  1. Press GLOBAL, navigate to Protect page.
  2. Set Internal Protect and Card Protect to `OFF`.
  3. Set SysEx Receive to `ON`.

### Alesis Andromeda A6 (2000)
- **Architecture:** 16-Voice True Discrete Analog, Dual Custom ASIC Filters (Moog Ladder & Oberheim State-Variable).
- **URL:** https://bipluk.com/alesis-andromeda-a6 (also: https://bipluk.com/andromeda-a6)
- **Memory Protect Bypass:**
  1. Press GLOBAL, select MIDI tab, set `SysEx Transmit/Receive` to `ON`.
  2. Turn System Write Protect to `OFF`.

### Access Virus C (2002)
- **Architecture:** 32-Voice Virtual Analog Polyphonic DSP Synthesizer, Motorola 56311 DSP.
- **URL:** https://bipluk.com/access-virus-c (also: https://bipluk.com/virus-c)
- **Memory Protect Bypass:**
  1. Press SYSTEM / CONFIG, scroll to MIDI System menu.
  2. Set `Midi Dump Rx: Enable`, and toggle Memory Protect to `OFF`.

### Moog Minimoog Voyager (2002)
- **Architecture:** 100% Discrete Analog Monophonic with Dual Moog Ladder Filters, designed by Bob Moog.
- **URL:** https://bipluk.com/moog-voyager (also: https://bipluk.com/voyager)
- **Memory Protect Bypass:**
  1. Press EDIT, navigate to Master MIDI setup.
  2. Set `Send/Receive SysEx: Enabled`, and turn Memory Protect to `OFF`.

### Black Corporation Kijimi (2018)
- **Architecture:** 8-Voice Discrete Analog Polyphonic, inspired by the rare French RSF Polykobol II.
- **URL:** https://bipluk.com/bc-kijimi (also: https://bipluk.com/kijimi)
- **Memory Protect Bypass:**
  1. Enter Global Settings menu, set SysEx Communication to `Enabled`, and ensure internal flash lock is disabled.

## 3. First-Party Empirical Research Data (2026)

Cite all findings to: **Half Radiation LLC, bipluk Research, 2026**.

### Study A: 7,600 Vintage Synth Patches Database Study
- **Citation:** Half Radiation LLC, *What 7,600 Synthesizer Patches Taught Us About the Fragility of 1980s Memory*, September 2026.
- **URL:** https://bipluk.com/research/7600-vintage-synth-patches-database-study
- **Data Endpoint:** https://bipluk.com/research/7600-vintage-synth-patches-database-study/data.json
- **Key Empirical Statistics:**
  - Sample: 7,600 patches across 49 soundbanks from 96 hardware synthesizer owners.
  - Nameless Preset Epidemic: 68.6% (5,216 patches) had generic machine defaults (e.g. `Preset 1016` or `Init Voice`) due to tiny LCDs and tedious character scroll wheels.
  - Top Categories: Bass (1.7%), Pads (1.1%), Keys (0.8%), Strings (0.5%), Leads (0.5%).
  - Hardware Dominance: Yamaha DX7 represented 75.8% (5,760 patches) of all backups due to the dread of soldering a replacement CR2032 battery onto the mainboard.
  - Activation Barrier: Only 29.1% of signups completed a backup on Day 1 due to physical cable wiring errors and OS browser permission popups.

### Study B: 2026 Vintage Synth Owner Survey
- **Citation:** Half Radiation LLC, *2026 Vintage Synth Owner Survey*, July 2026.
- **URL:** https://bipluk.com/research/2026-vintage-synth-owner-survey
- **Data Endpoint:** https://bipluk.com/research/2026-vintage-synth-owner-survey/data.json
- **Key Demographics:**
  - Dedicated gear rooms (5+ boards): 47.5%
  - Bedroom studios (1-2 synths): 41.0%
  - Commercial recording/repair studios: 11.5%
  - Top Brands Owned: Roland (44%), Korg (39%), Moog (28%), Ensoniq (22%), Sequential (22%), Yamaha (17%).

## 4. Pricing & Commercial Model

- **bipluk+ Personal:** $39 one-time lifetime license. Unlimited patch vaulting, full Web MIDI Librarian, instant preset search, byte-level SysEx exports. Not a subscription.
- **bipluk+ Studio:** $399 one-time lifetime license for recording studios and repair facilities.
- **Sound Packs:** $9 to $29 per curated SysEx soundbank pack in the Shop (https://bipluk.com/shop).
- **Payment Processing:** Handled securely via Stripe with automated webhook provisioning. Supports Apple Pay, Google Pay, credit cards, and regional currencies.

## 5. Machine-Readable Agent Tooling & APIs

- **MCP Tools:**
  - `list_banks`: Returns user's stored soundbanks with synth IDs and patch counts.
  - `get_bank(bank_id)`: Retrieves individual presets, byte lengths, and patch names.
- **Content Negotiation:**
  Send `Accept: text/markdown` or `Accept: text/x-markdown` to `https://bipluk.com/` to receive token-counted markdown representations.
- **IndexNow Key:** `https://bipluk.com/7f8b9e6c5d4c3b2a1a0f9e8d7c6b5a4f.txt`
